title: Uptime Alliance handoff canvas — cross-functional SLO delivery (90d)
content:
Summary:
This is a working 'handoff canvas' for the Uptime Alliance: a 90-day cross-functional initiative to align serving-runtime, platform-engineering, and feature teams on stable SLOs, measurement, and operational handoffs for model-serving. The doc is intentionally lightweight — treat as a scratchpad + contract for the first 90 days.

Purpose & scope:
- Purpose: define minimal, testable SLOs for model serving and create clear handoff artifacts (dashboards, runbooks, alert contracts) so teams can operate without firefighting.
- Scope: hosted API routes and Dedicated pools for text-generation and embeddings, plus the routing/fallback logic. Private deployments are out-of-scope for the initial 90d (target later wave).

High-level goals (90 days):
1) Instrumentation parity: ensure all production serving routes emit the same SLI schema by day 30.
2) Baseline SLOs: provisional SLOs agreed by day 45 and implemented in alerting by day 60.
3) Handoff bundle: per-service runbook + escalation matrix + canary plan published by day 75.
4) Trial: run a 2-week reliability trial (small set of feature teams) and collect signals for final SLO tuning by day 90.

Provisional SLI / SLO proposals (for team discussion):
- Availability SLO: 99.95% measured as successful request rate (status 2xx / 5xx+4xx) per route per week.
- Latency SLO (generation routes): P95 < 120 ms for short context (<= 512 tokens), P95 < 350 ms for long context (> 512 tokens).
- Error budget guardrail: if error budget consumption > 40% in a 7-day window trigger dedicated war-room and an auto-fallback policy to lower-cost variant.
- Quality SLO (applied for regen/rerank flows): baseline acceptance rate of top-N responses measured via eval-set A/B probes >= 96% of baseline model.
Notes: these numbers are provisional; plan includes an A/B experiment to validate user-impact before finalizing.

Measurement signals (what to emit):
- request.latency_ms (histogram)
- request.status_code (counter)
- model.fallback_triggered (counter with reason tag)
- kvcache.hit_ratio (gauge)
- batching.batch_size (histogram)
- tokens.generated (counter)
- per-route user-facing error_tix (counter aggregated to SRE-ops dashboard)

Owners & handoff matrix:
- Serving-runtime: implementation of SLI schema + optimized kernels. Primary owner: Ethan Zhao.
- Platform-engineering: alerting pipelines, dashboards, dedicated pool autoscaler rules. Primary owner: Priya Nair.
- SRE: SLO definitions, dashboard templates, runbook scaffold. Primary owner: Maya Patel (doc lead) + Liam O'Connor (oncall integration).
- Feature teams (sample): notifications-service, chat-ui, search-ranking. Responsible for validating UX impact and participating in trial.

Handoff artifacts (deliverables):
- Per-route SLI schema file (JSON schema) and instrumented agent libs (serving-runtime client).
- Shared dashboard templates (Grafana/Observability) for P95/P99, error rates, kvcache, batch size.
- Runbook bundle: incident checklist, run-level play (how to triage a fallback loop), rollback plan, postmortem template.
- Canary recipe + traffic split template (how to route 2%->10%->50%).
- Automated smoke tests for SLI verification executed by CI on merges to main.

Proposed timeline (milestones):
- Week 0 (kickoff): cross-team alignment workshop, agree on owner list, create base Confluence page (this doc).
- Week 1–4 (instrumentation sprint): implement SLI schema + library updates; small feature teams validate locally.
- Week 5–7 (SLO & alerts sprint): agree provisional SLOs, create alerting rules, wire dashboards.
- Week 8–10 (handoff artifacts sprint): write runbooks, define canary recipes, create postmortem template.
- Week 11–12 (trial & tuning): run trial with 2–3 feature teams, collect data, adjust thresholds, finalize SLOs.

Decision criteria for finalizing SLOs:
- No more than 10% negative user-impact measured in A/B trial for latency adjustments.
- Dashboards show stable telemetry (noise/reduction in false positives) for 7 consecutive days.
- Ops runbooks exercised in at least 1 simulated incident.

Communication & cadence:
- Weekly alignment sync: Thu 10:00 AM PT — stakeholder review (30m).
- Bi-weekly deep dive: Wed 2:00 PM PT — data review (1h).
- Slack channel: #sre-uptime-alliance (owner: Maya Patel). Use thread for every incident/test.
- Quarterly exec note: short summary for VP-eng (~1 page) after day 90.

Playlists (tactical checklist, living):
- [ ] Add SLI schema to serving-runtime repo (ENG-9876). Owner: Ethan. Target: 2026-03-15.
- [ ] Build Grafana template for per-route SLOs. Owner: Priya. Target: 2026-03-22.
- [ ] Create runbook scaffold (incident->triage->mitigation->postmortem). Owner: Liam. Target: 2026-03-29.
- [ ] Configure alerting to send to #sre-uptime-alliance and paging. Owner: Priya. Target: 2026-04-05.
- [ ] Run simulated degraded-network incident and exercise runbook. Owner: feature team leads. Target: 2026-04-12.

Experiment ideas to reduce noise and improve SLO economics:
- Dynamic batching aggressiveness ramp: measure latency/throughput tradeoff at 4, 8, 16 token bundle sizes.
- Adaptive kvcache eviction policy based on request patterns per route (probing small set of routes).
- Cost-aware routing: prefer smaller quantized variants for non-critical paths and verify quality SLO via shadow evals.

Known risks & mitigations:
- Risk: inconsistent telemetry across services -> Mitigation: small compatibility shim and one-week retro with SDK owners.
- Risk: alert fatigue from overly-sensitive rules -> Mitigation: use burn-rate and composite alerts, run two-week tuning window.
- Risk: fallback cascade under heavy load -> Mitigation: implement circuit-breaker at router layer and canary fallback thresholds.

Runbook excerpt (short):
- Trigger: route error rate > 0.1% for 5m AND error budget consumption > 20% in 24h.
- Immediate: open incident, tag #sre-uptime-alliance, page oncall SRE, collect last 1hr traces and top-10 failing requests.
- Triage: confirm whether root cause is model (timeouts, memory), infra (GPU OOM, autoscaler thrash), or routing (fallback storms).
- Mitigate: depending on cause — scale Dedicated pool, revert recent deploy, enable model-variant fallback, or pause unsafe autoscaler rules.

Postmortem template (required fields):
- Summary (1–2 lines), Timeline, Impact (customers, routes), Root-cause analysis, Actions (short/long-term), Owner for each action, Validation plan.

Open questions / decisions needed this week:
1) Finalize whether availability SLO should exclude planned maintenance windows or roll into maintenance SLO — ops preference: exclude scheduled windows if >48h notice.
2) Determine how to express quality SLOs for embeddings (cosine-similarity threshold vs downstream task metric).
3) Agree on minimum telemetry retention for SLO backfills (30 days recommended).

Appendix: useful links & references
- Confluence Uptime Alliance overview (linked above).
- Quick checklist for SDK authors: emit histogram with these tag names: route, model_id, region, variant.
- Example Jira tickets to watch: SRE-4212 (dashboard template), ENG-9876 (SLI schema), SERV-412 (fallback routing change).

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc as the "single source" for the first 90d — we will formalize into a larger playbook later.
- Expect pushback from feature teams about strict P95 targets; plan to use trial data as bargaining chip.
- Call out a small set of 'pilot routes' early (e.g., chat-generate-v1, embeddings-search-v2) to reduce blast radius.

If you're editing this doc: add your name to collaborators and update the playlist with deadlines.
